Fixed in cbac06c38. The balance now sums each row as its money field submits it, rounded to the row's precision. Three `-100/3` rows leave -0.01, and submit stays disabled. A system test covers this.

Fixed in cbac06c38. `money_field_value` rejects exponents beyond ±20. It counts decimals from the significant digits and the exponent, so nothing is expanded to plain notation. Helper tests cover `1e-1000000000` and `1e1000000000`.

Fixed in cbac06c38. A switch made while a lookup is still unresolved keeps the first snapshot. The latest lookup clears it when it lands or fails. A system test switches JPY → EUR → USD with `1.234` typed in between and expects `1.23`.

Fixed in cbac06c38. Both fields get an explicit precision when the saved balance has more decimals than the currency. Otherwise they keep following the currency picker. A controller test renders a JPY statement with 100.25 and 1500.

Fixed in cbac06c38. The precision is the saved value's decimals, at least 2, so `123.456` renders unchanged. Covered by a controller test.

Fixed in cbac06c38. An existing target shows its own currency, and a new account shows the family currency. Precision stays at least 2, so switching Destination before saving still accepts decimals.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Intended. The rows round to the total's precision because `Entry#split!` needs them to add up to the parent exactly. The field shows the rounded value as soon as it is left, so `0.3333` becomes `0.33` on screen before submit. With the fix above, the remaining balance uses the same rounded values. Rows keep up to four decimals when the total has them, for example an imported 80.4 JPY total.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Intended. Rounding to the account currency is how the shared money field works everywhere, including the transaction form's amount, and making that uniform is the point of this PR. The value is not dropped silently: the field shows the rounded value as soon as it is left, so `0.004` reads `0.00` before submit. A sub-cent fee or a four-decimal USD transfer is not something a bank account records.
